wants: A nineteenth-century cofradía book or pastoral visitation from Spanish America or Brazil, for continuity beyond Mexico
drafter_flags: The inventory missed this: the text's 'much older popular Catholicism' and the confraternities and feasts that 'carried on much as before' name the colonial devotional world.

The evidence is Mexican and about one devotion (Guadalupe); it shows the later church taking up a colonial devotion and its colonial book as its own. A reviewer may judge Documented too high for a continent-wide continuity and prefer Inferential-Thin.
De la Rosa is a canon of Guadalajara cathedral (lines 109-117); the note calls him 'a priest'. The era-8 text does not name this relationship, so it is not era 8's.
links.change_reason: New link: the colonial devotional church carried into the nineteenth-century republics, named in the Latin American text.

prose_changes.old: The Union of Utrecht is still there: a small communion of national churches in the Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Poland and the Czech lands. Its most consequential work turned out to be ecumenical. The Bonn conferences Dollinger convened in the 1870s were among the first modern meetings of Old Catholic, Anglican and Orthodox theologians at one table, and in 1931 the Old Catholics and the Church of England entered full communion by the Bonn Agreement — one of the earliest such agreements between separated Western churches, and a model for many since.
prose_changes.new: The Union of Utrecht is still there. It is a small family of national churches in the Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Poland and the Czech lands. Its most lasting work turned out to be ecumenical. In 1874 and 1875 Dollinger called meetings at Bonn that brought Old Catholic, Anglican and Orthodox theologians to one table. Their theses were a first attempt to set down the faith all three held in common. In 1931 the Old Catholics and the Church of England entered full communion by the Bonn Agreement.
prose_changes.reason: Removed 'one of the earliest such agreements between separated Western churches, and a model for many since' (no vendored or repo-cited source). 'Among the first modern meetings' restated as Schaff's 'first attempt to formularize the doctrinal consensus of Old Catholics, Greeks, and Anglo-Catholics' (Schaff vol. 2, lines 43852-43854). Split for readability.

prose_changes.old: Schism from Rome across the whole post-independence period (verified — no Rome-trained clergy; the state runs the church; the Catholic-Vodou creole field forms in the vacuum); the Concordat signed 28 Mar 1860 (verified) — the story’s own resolution; start 1804 precedes the era once, disclosed (the story is indivisible)
prose_changes.new: Haiti's church was cut off from Rome for the whole time after independence in 1804. Almost no priests trained under Rome arrived, and the state ran the church. In that gap a religious life that joined Catholic and Vodou practice took shape. A concordat signed on 28 March 1860 ended the break.
prose_changes.reason: The field was internal verification and era-placement language ('verified', 'disclosed', 'the story is indivisible'). Rewritten in plain words with the same facts, which the longDescription already states.

prose_changes.old: This is the century that made Latin America's church what it is: a Roman-aligned hierarchy laid over a much older popular Catholicism, with far fewer priests per head than Europe had, and a long habit of arguing with the state. The 1899 council was the first time the continent's bishops met as a single body, and the continental conferences that followed — Rio in 1955, Medellin in 1968 — grew from that precedent. Latin America is still home to the largest share of the world's Catholics.
prose_changes.new: This is the century that made Latin America's church what it is: a Roman-aligned hierarchy laid over a much older popular Catholicism, with far fewer priests per head than Europe had, and a long habit of arguing with the state. The 1899 council in Rome was the first time the continent's bishops met as a single body. They met again as a continent at Rio in 1955 and at Medellin in 1968. Latin America is still home to the largest share of the world's Catholics.
prose_changes.reason: 'The continental conferences that followed ... grew from that precedent' is a causal claim with no vendored or repo-cited source; restated as a sequence of meetings.

escalations: Several no-entry facts have no vendored or repo-cited source but are not in doubt: the 1850 English hierarchy, the US immigrant church, Rerum Novarum, Mexico's Reform laws, Rome's slow recognition of the republics, and Old Catholic celibacy and vernacular reforms. I left them as written and listed them in wants rather than hedge settled facts with 'may have'. Mark to rule whether that is right.

Four fields carry sentence fragments that need more than a one-sentence fix and were not touched: Catholic 19th c. longDescription ('Weeks before Italian troops...'), Old Catholic longDescription ('And then went on to drop...'), Haitian longDescription ('Some genuine priests...', 'And began a much longer argument...'), Latin American longDescription ('Sharpest in Mexico...'). These are full-paragraph rewrites.
